transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira (AE), Jordan (SE), Maya (CSM) — Evan (VP Eng), Priya (Head of Data), Liam (IT)

Summary (auto): quick intro, technical intake for VPC/on-prem networking and pilot plan.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira, AE on the account, and with me are Jordan our solutions engineer and Maya on CSM. Evan, Priya, Liam thanks for making time.
[00:12] Evan: Yeah thanks. Quick note — we put this on to make sure the networking side is covered before pilot. We've got some compliance folks that'll want to see audit logs and key management.
[00:22] Maya: great, that's exactly what we want to align on today. We'll cover networking, peering, and a rough pilot success criteria.
[00:29] Jordan: hi all — I'll take the technical questions. Quick q: are you planning to use our hosted API or do you already expect dedicated/private deployment?
[00:38] Priya: short term we want hosted for eval, but our compliance team is pushing for dedicated or VPC peering for anything with PII. So pilot probably needs to exercise dedicated flow.
[00:48] Samira: okay that maps to our standard path; we'll show you the dedicated options and the VPC peering model, plus how audit logs and KMS integrations look.
[00:56] Liam: on the networking side, we need details about NAT traversal, keep-alive, and socket behavior, also ports we need to open. We also run a few on-prem firewall appliances that might rewrite headers, so we want to avoid brittle setups.
[01:12] Jordan: noted. For peering we usually need a route table exchange and one or two TCP ports for gRPC or TLS — we can work with firewall team. There are also recommendations about MTU and idle timeouts — will send checklist.
[01:27] Evan: perfect. Also raise the question of egress costs in dedicated. We run chat-heavy workloads and tokens are high, so cost profile matters.
[01:36] Samira: we'll include a cost comparison doc — hosted vs dedicated with traffic assumptions. We'll also show batching and quantization levers that reduce per-token cost.
[01:45] Priya: good. On KMS — we need HSM-backed key wrapping and retention policy for audit readiness.
[01:52] Jordan: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. There are some caveats around key rotation windows for live KV cache encryption; I'll flag those.
[02:06] Liam: could you remind me how data at rest is handled in Dedicated? We have to prove that customer data is isolated and not commingled.
[02:13] Jordan: Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated; we provide disk-level encryption and separate namespaces for KV caches. But if you need air-gapped, we have private on-prem packaging as well — that's a heavier lift but doable.
[02:26] Evan: timeline question — if we start pilot mid-May, how fast can you spin up a dedicated pool or will we run against hosted with a VPC peering sim?
[02:36] Samira: typical Dedicated spin-up is 2–4 weeks depending on capacity and contracts. For pilot we often do hosted with a dedicated routing policy and network isolation via VPC peering to simulate production. That gets you to meaningful perf data quickly.
[02:51] Priya: okay that helps. Liam, any specific firewall vendor/version notes?
[02:56] Liam: we're Palo Alto and Forti in some regions, sometimes an F5 in front. We do TLS interception in a couple of branches which may break mutual TLS.
[03:06] Jordan: that's important — mutual TLS is fragile if interception occurs. We can switch to mTLS over port X and certificate pinning, but if interception is present you'll need to exempt Redwood endpoints. I'll add that to the checklist.
[03:18] Maya: action: Jordan will validate TLS path and provide recommended exemption rules.
[03:23] Samira: also to be clear on compliance — we'll share SOC2 plus the architecture diagrams. If you need ISO or specific audit artifacts, we'll get them from security.
[03:34] Evan: yes please. Our procurement will also want the SLA and data retention specifics.
[03:40] Samira: noted, I'll include SLA details and retention policy in the pack.
[03:44] Priya: for pilot metrics, can we instrument latency P95 and per-token cost per route?
[03:49] Jordan: yes we surface token-level cost and latency in the Console. For pilot we'll set up a dashboard and trace hooks for your devs. We'll also set up a small eval dataset to monitor quality drift.
[04:02] Evan: cool. One other nuance — we need to test long-context behavior, like 8k sequences. Are the Dedicated pools tuned for that?
[04:11] Jordan: our runtime supports configurable kernel selection and KV cache handling; for long contexts we pick kernels and larger KV handling. There is a performance vs cost tradeoff; we'll provide guidance on sequence-length bucketization and batching.
[04:26] Liam: any special network tuning for large KV exchange? We want to avoid timeouts during cold-starts.
[04:32] Jordan: yes — larger sequences increase initial payloads; keep-alive and larger initial timeout windows recommended. We'll add a suggested NGINX/tcp keepalive config.
[04:43] Priya: sounds thorough. For the pilot success criteria, suggested items: accuracy on a labeled prompt set, latency under 500ms P95, and cost per 1k tokens under $X.
[04:55] Maya: I'll draft a formal success criteria doc with those metrics and circulate.
[05:01] Samira: great. On commercial terms we usually offer a 30-day pilot with a usage cap plus optional Dedicated trial credits. We'll outline options in the pricing sheet.
[05:11] Evan: procurement will want contract language about data residency. We keep EU customers in EU region.
[05:17] Samira: absolutely — we can pin region and provide private control plane options for Private deployments.
[05:23] Liam: security question — do you support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC for routes?
[05:28] Jordan: yes SAML SSO and RBAC are available, and you can restrict routes by token-level permissions. We'll share the integration playbook.
[05:36] Evan: can you demo the Console later? We might want to see the per-route telemetry.
[05:40] Samira: we can schedule a focused Console demo — Maya, let's find a slot next week.
[05:44] Maya: will do.
[05:46] Jordan: quick note about fallback behavior — if a Dedicated node fails we'll automatically route to a compatible hosted model unless you opt out. That provides graceful degradation.
[05:57] Priya: that's acceptable as long as logs show the fallback and we can audit each routed request.
[06:03] Jordan: yes the trace hooks include fallback flags and model version metadata.
[06:08] Evan: any concerns about model drift during pilot? We run frequent prompt changes.
[06:12] Jordan: we'll set up quality monitoring tied to your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can alert regressions and suggest model/quantization adjustments.
[06:22] Priya: perfect. For the network baseline, what exact artifacts will you need from us?
[06:26] Jordan: ideally a list of egress CIDRs, firewall rules, NAT gateways, and any TLS interception appliances with config snippets. Also a low-level network diagram would help.
[06:37] Liam: I'll export an internal diagram and share — might redact some IPs.
[06:41] Samira: that's fine, anything that helps us produce the checklist is useful.
[06:46] Evan: ok logistics — pilot kickoff week of May 19th works for us.
[06:50] Maya: I'll propose three slots after the call.
[06:53] Samira: action recap: Samira send pricing and contract options; Jordan send network checklist and TLS exceptions; Maya create pilot success doc and calendar invite.
[07:05] Priya: are there any integrations for our existing observability stack? We use Datadog and Splunk.
[07:12] Jordan: audit logs and metrics can be forwarded to Datadog and Splunk via our log forwarder or S3 export — we'll include setup steps.
[07:22] Evan: for the pilot dataset, we plan to include customer tickets and anonymized transcripts — is that supported?
[07:29] Samira: yes, you'll be able to upload prompt sets and sample transcripts; we'll advise on sanitization best practices.
[07:36] Liam: small note — some of our branches have strict egress policies. Do you have a VPN-based alternative?
[07:42] Jordan: yes for strict environments we can do private peering or an on-prem box variant that acts as a gateway — that's in our Private offering and requires additional setup.
[07:53] Evan: fine, for pilot we won't use on-prem, but we might test the VPN/gateway in a later phase.
[07:59] Maya: I'll capture that as a potential later milestone.
[08:04] Samira: anything else from the Palisade team?
[08:06] Priya: nothing else.
[08:08] Liam: no.
[08:09] Evan: good, thanks all.
[08:11] Samira: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and invites.

Notes: transcript contains some short overlaps and mislabels common to automated transcription — a few words like "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache" or "kv cash".

Action items (inline):
- Jordan Lee: network checklist, TLS exemption rules, keepalive/MTU recommendations (due 2025-05-14)
- Samira Patel: pricing sheet, SLA & retention docs, contract options (due 2025-05-12)
- Maya Chen: pilot success criteria doc, calendar invites for kickoff week of 2025-05-19 (due 2025-05-13)

End of transcript.
